correctness.rationale: The spherical football F_alpha has longitude period 2πα with a=πα<π; the nearest longitude separation δ∈[0,a] is uniform. The intrinsic spherical cosine formula makes opposite pole pairs the sole diameter contacts for any fixed α<1. With colatitudes s=εu, t=εv, the positive-quadrant form Q=u²+v²+2uv cosδ is uniformly coercive at fixed a<π; dominated convergence yields fourth-order tail (2a)^−1∫_0^a I(cosδ)dδ. Polar substitution gives I(cosδ)=(sinδ−δcosδ)/(8sin³δ), integral C=[csc²a−cot(a)/a]/32. I increases strictly in δ, hence its running average is strictly increasing from 1/48 to infinity; α=1 sphere separately has ε²/4. Independent angular quadrature at α=.1,.25,.5,.75,.9 agrees, including nonorbifold α>.5.
residual_risks: At α↑1 local domination ceases uniformly and the exponent changes; do not interchange ε and α limits; only curvature +1 and equal cone angles with 0<α<1.
